**[[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]

{{Quote|Supreme Chancellor, delegates of the Senate, a tragedy has occurred, which started right here with the taxation of trade routes, and has now engulfed our entire planet in the oppression of the Trade Federation!|[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]|<ref name="SWEI:TPM" />}}
The '''Trade Federation''', also known as the '''Trade Federation of Planets''' or '''Galactic Trade Federation''', was a shipping conglomerate established in [[350 BBY/Legends|350 BBY]] to mediate disputes between shipping firms.<ref name="TEGTAS" /> By the [[100 BBY/Legends|100s BBY]], it had evolved into a powerful commerce guild, trade cartel, megacorporation, and lobbying group in its own right as an association of business and trade groups, with its own large [[Trade Federation Merchant Fleet|commercial trade fleet]].<ref name="SON">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref>

The Federation grew to dominate entire [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] and all major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade routes]], and possessed a formidable [[Trade Defense Force|private military]] and [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|droid army]]. Towards the end of the Republic, it would become increasingly dominated by the commerce-savvy [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]]. Its immense influence made it the favored pawn of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], who manipulated [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] to stoke dissatisfaction in the systems controlled by the Federation, sowing the seeds for a [[Clone Wars/Legends|war]] that would destroy the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Under Gunray's leadership, the Trade Federation was responsible for the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockade]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] in protest against [[Senate Resolution BR-0371|increased taxation]].<ref name="SWEI:TPM" /> After its defeat at Naboo, the Trade Federation and numerous other megacorporations sided with [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] movement out of fear of nationalization by the Republic.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref><ref name="SWEII:AOTC" />

Again under Sidious' influence, the Federation played a major role in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and its large droid army and fleet formed the core of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|CIS military]]. Unbeknownst to the CIS, Sidious's alter ego, Palpatine, was the Chancellor of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], which allowed him to control the war on both ends and deceive both the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and Separatists. In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Sidious [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|betrayed]] Gunray and the CIS, and orchestrated the CIS's destruction. Under the brief leadership of its final Viceroy, [[Sentepeth Findos]], the Trade Federation was [[Imperialization/Legends|imperialized]] by Sidious' new [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. A [[Trade Federation resistance|small remnant]] led by [[Marath Vooro]] continued resistance for several months until its defeat in the [[Five Veils Campaign]]. The Trade Federation itself was not officially disbanded until the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] was [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|dissolved]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="RHNSIE" />

==History==
===Pre-Clone Wars===
====Idealistic origins====
{{Quote|You have to understand what these sectors were like before the Trade Federation arrived. And if it were made to leave? Then there'd be no law at all.|[[Firmus Kett]] reflects on the Trade Federation's early history|<ref name="EGW-cut6" />}}
The Trade Federation of Planets was founded during the [[Golden Age of the Old Republic]] in the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] in [[350 BBY/Legends|350 BBY]] as a [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]-charted organization tasked with mediating disputes between [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] merchants and shipping firms. At the [[Time/Legends|time]], transportation [[Megacorporation/Legends|megacorporations]] such as [[Pulsar Supertanker]], [[Quasar Cargo]], [[Red Star Shipping Lines]], and [[Ororo Transportation/Legends|Ororo Transportation]] were stifling commerce by shutting out competitors from [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] and refusing to share navigational data. The Trade Federation, initially composed of many [[Species/Legends|species]], including the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]], helped curb such abuses, and within a hundred years had become a powerful shipping cartel in its own right.<ref name="TEGtW" /> The Federation was originally controlled by a [[Trade Federation Directorate|directorate]], which was led by a commanding [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]].<ref name="E:ICS">''[[Star Wars: Episode I Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

The Trade Federation's members increasingly worked together to negotiate more favorable rates and policies, and also contracted with [[Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc./Legends|Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc.]] to build a [[Trade Federation Merchant Fleet|new fleet]] of [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|LH-3210 cargo freighters]]. By [[250 BBY/Legends|250 BBY]], the Trade Federation had advanced beyond its original mission and had become a powerful association lobbying to advance trade interests in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. It also worked to open up new regions of the galaxy to trade and commerce, with the [[Trade Explorer Corps]] blazing numerous new routes into the Outer Rim and establishing networks of retail outlets, depots, waystations and landing fields in thousands of isolated systems.<ref name="TEGtW" />

As its power grew, the Trade Federation found itself having to defend its transports from [[Pirate/Legends|piracy]]. Rather than rely on corrupt or ineffectual [[Planetary Security Forces]], the Federation established its own [[Trade Defense Force]], which became a capable and well-regarded paramilitary that earned the respect and admiration of the Republic's [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]].<ref name="TEGtW" />

The Trade Federation of the late [[200 BBY/Legends|200s BBY]] was seen by many as the ideal Republic institution: run by a diverse group of species and interests, it represented its members capably and fairly on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], made investments that advanced commerce across the galaxy, and augmented the power of the Judicials and Planetary Security Forces with the Trade Defense Force.<ref name="TEGtW" /> And illustrative example can be seen in the [[Rseik sector/Legends|Rseik sector]] in [[214 BBY]]: the sector had an endemic problem with piracy, and in the aftermath of the [[Bordal Contagion]], the firms [[Kett Shipping]], [[Rseikharhl Hullspace]], [[Cotellieri Transports Limited]], and the [[Ma'ar Shaddam Weaponsmiths Guild]] decided to approach the Trade Federation for aid. Following a secret meeting with a [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorran]] Federation agent on the planet [[Syned]], all parties agreed to become Federation subsidiaries. The Federation moved in a [[Flotilla/Legends|flotilla]] of [[Gunboat/Legends|gunboats]] and [[Patrol ship/Legends|system patrol craft]] via [[Svivren/Legends|Svivren]], along with with a pair of [[Munifex-class light cruiser|''Munifex''-class light cruisers]] and a [[Captor-class heavy munitions cruiser|''Captor''-class heavy munitions cruiser]]. On their first convoy escort to [[Kabal/Legends|Kabal]], they were ambushed by the [[Fujari]] pirates at [[Tertiary Fujar system/Legends|Tertiary Fujar]]. In the course of an hour, the Fujari pirates and their [[Fujari asteroid base|asteroid base]] were completely destroyed by the [[Trade Defense Force]]. A week later the TDF destroyed the [[Hajara gang|Hajara pirate gang]]. Within a decade the Trade Federation had upgraded spaceport facilities at [[Kirdo III/Legends|Kirdo III]] and [[Laria]], established a depot for goods at [[Tyne Albamon]], blazed a faster route to Svivren, and installed a TDF marine post at the [[Dravian Starport]]. By that time, Kett Shipping was running more than twenty convoys a year without a single loss.<ref name="EGW-cut6" />

====Cartelization====
As its power grew, the Trade Federation became a cartel in its own right, dominating galactic trade and ruthlessly suppressing opposition. By [[150 BBY/Legends|150 BBY]], trade between the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]] and the Rim was once again drying up. In an effort to jump-start commerce, the Galactic Senate declared the entire Outer Rim a [[Free Trade Zone/Legends|Free Trade Zone]] in [[124 BBY]], but this merely exempted the Trade Federation from local taxation. It moved aggressively into the new Free Trade Zone, crafting arrangements with impoverished sectors that effectively handed over their Senate votes. Other sectors were forced to give up their economic self-determination, becoming perpetual customers for the Trade Federation.<ref name="TEGtW" /> The Trade Federation held maps of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] routes closely rather than sharing them, enabling them to cement their hold over trade routes. Only the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the Office of the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] were able to maintain maps of similar quality. The Federation had many planetary protectorates throughout the galaxy, often using the ceremonial halls inside their core ships to sign protectorship agreements.<ref name="AOTC:ICS">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

Within two generations, the Trade Federation controlled enough Senate votes to hamper competitors, influence the courts, and stall legislation. In [[67 BBY/Legends|67 BBY]] it even gained a seat in the Senate on the same level as a member world as a [[functional constituency]], represented by [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]].<ref name="SWEI:TPM" /> The Trade Federation gained full voting privileges as part of a deal secretly negotiated by [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Hego Damask II]] of [[Damask Holdings/Legends|Damask Holdings]], the ''alter ego'' of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], in which they accepted the reform of the Free Trade Zones in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], even though this would cost some of their shipping monopoly and expose them to competition from start-up companies. Though the Trade Federation gained representation in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] in exchange, the leadership remained disgruntled at the loss of some of its monopoly.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

In [[65 BBY/Legends|65 BBY]], the Trade Federation gained full rights to construct a [[Theed Spaceport/Legends|new spaceport]] for [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] on the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], and to export the planet's newly-discovered [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] resources: as Hego Damask, Darth Plagueis explicitly involved the Trade Federation to reconcile them to the earlier [[Free Trade Zone/Legends|Free Trade Zone Deal]]. Many on Naboo, however, especially isolationists like [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Vidar Kim]], pointed out that the Trade Federation would sell Naboo's plasma on for ten or even twenty times what it paid for it, and saw the deal as unjust and exploitative.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Between [[59 BBY/Legends|59 BBY]] and [[56 BBY/Legends|56 BBY]]<ref name="Discovery">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' states that after the [[discovery of Alaris Prime]] of [[Alaris Prime/Legends|Alaris Prime]], the explorers who found it petitioned the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] for rights to colonize it, which were [[Alaris Prime colonization resolution|resolved]] after twenty [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of debate. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' states that the [[Colonist/Legends|colonization]] of Alaris Prime took place between [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]] and [[36 BBY/Legends|36 BBY]], indicating that the [[Moon/Legends|moon's]] discovery took place between [[59 BBY/Legends|59 BBY]] and [[56 BBY/Legends|56 BBY]].</ref> the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Alaris Prime/Legends|Alaris Prime]] in the [[Kashyyyk system/Legends|Kashyyyk system]] was [[Discovery of Alaris Prime|rediscovered]] by [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] explorers from the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], who petitioned the Senate for the rights to [[Colonist/Legends|colonize]] it. The Trade Federation expressed its own interest in the moon, desiring its abundant resources and hoping to create a trade center there between Kashyyyk, [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]], and [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]].<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

Many on Coruscant bemoaned the Trade Federation's corruption, predatory business practices, and the extinction of representation for the systems it controlled. When Senator Vidar Kim was assassinated by a never-identified [[Maladian]] gunman at the behest of Darth Plagueis, many were prepared to suggest that the Trade Federation had in fact been responsible.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> However, others admired it for the TDF's rapid extinction of piracy on the major hyperlanes. A terrorist group known as the [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]] declared its intention to fight the Trade Federation by any means necessary, while the [[Stark Commercial Combine]] led by [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]] began raiding Trade Federation convoys and selling pirated goods for a huge markup. In this period, the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] faction became increasingly influential in the Trade Federation. The Neimoidians who ran the Trade Federation received their organizational skills from running mass hives and fungus farms on their homeworld of [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]] and the Neimoidian [[Purse world/Legends|purse worlds]] like [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], [[Deko Neimoidia/Legends|Deko Neimoidia]], and [[Koru Neimoidia/Legends|Koru Neimoidia]].<ref name="CNITDB">{{DB|location|catoneimoidia|Cato Neimoidia}}</ref>

====The Stark Hyperspace War====
The [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]] of [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]] was a turning point for both the Trade Federation and its opponents in the Senate: amid a [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] shortage, Iaco Stark began raiding Trade Federation bacta shipments and selling them on for reduced prices, becoming a hero to many in the Outer Rim. In response, the Trade Federation demanded the right to greater armaments on its merchant ships. However, what appeared to be a simple smuggler conflict was in fact a ruse cooked up between Stark, the [[Xucphra Corporation|Xucphra]] bacta corporation, and [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Hask]], who saw it as an opportunity to cripple the Republic's military forces with Stark's [[navcomputer virus]] and so between them achieve economic domination over the galaxy.<ref name="TEGtW" />

Senator [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] called for a peace conference to address the underlying causes of the war. However, aware that the Trade Federation had conspired with Xucphra to manufacture the bacta shortage, and believing that only force would resolve the conflict, Senator [[Ranulph Tarkin/Legends|Ranulph Tarkin]] blackmailed Trade Federation Minister [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] into revealing the conference's location on [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]]. Assembling a [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|fleet]], Tarkin raced to Troiken to ambush Stark's forces, but his fleet was decimated by Stark's navcomputer virus and he was forced to go to ground on the planet. As bitter attritional fighting developed on Troiken, a Jedi task force discovered Xucphra and the Trade Federation's conspiracy. On Coruscant, Jedi Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] used the information to intimidate Viceroy Hask and Nute Gunray into releasing TDF assets for a counterattack. Stark defected to the Republic and helped end the crisis in exchange for amnesty, but both the Trade Federation and its opponents in the Senate had been radicalized. Hask resigned over the conspiracy and was replaced as Viceroy by Nute Gunray, and the Trade Federation intensified its demands for greater protection on its merchant ships.<ref name="TEGtW" /><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref><ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

The entire crisis had in fact been orchestrated by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] to [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] and publicly [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Sidious used the crisis to intensify tensions between the Core Worlds and the Outer Rim systems dominated by the Trade Federation. He would continue manipulating the Trade Federation and its enemies until the galaxy stood on the brink of a [[Clone Wars/Legends|war]] that would destroy the Republic.<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TEA" />

====Under the Neimoidians====
{{Quote|I realize that your voracious desires stem from the cruel conditions of your upbringing&mdash;you and your fellow grubs in ruthless competition for limited supplies of fungus. But I understand. We are all shaped by our infantile desires, our longing for affection and attention, our fears of death. And judging by how far you have come, it's clear that you were unrivaled and continue to be.|[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] declares himself to Viceroy [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]].|<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />}}
[[File:Pirate_Attack.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Pirates attack a Trade Federation merchant ship]]
Over the next decade, the [[Neimoidian Inner Circle]] became increasingly influential in the seven-member [[Trade Federation Directorate]], though the Federation only became a Neimoidian monopoly in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], when six other members of the Trade Federation Directorate were murdered, leaving only Viceroy [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]].<ref name="COD" /> During this time, the Trade Federation also started building up a droid invasion army in secret. In order to ensure the creation and mobilization of the army was kept secret from the authorities at the Galactic Republic, they referred to the suspicious pieces of equipment as being shipments of the most expensive and latest rendition of [[Binary loadlifter/Legends|binary loadlifters]] when undergoing checks by the [[Republic Customs Office]].<ref name="SW:CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> The Federation's growing power and influence led many in the Senate to consider re-imposing taxation on the Outer Rim, effectively abolishing the Free Trade Zones. The Trade Federation was invariably opposed to renewed taxation, and through its senator, [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]], endlessly filibustered Senate debates on the issue.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

=====Alaris Prime=====
{{Quote|We've gained knowledge of Trade Federation activity on Alaris. But where there is one battle droid, there is frequently an army.|[[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]|<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>}}
After two [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] of debate the rights to Alaris Prime were [[Alaris Prime colonization resolution|awarded]] to the Wookiees, a ruling the Trade Federation ignored by sending part of the Droid Army to launch an illegal colony on the moon<ref name="GB" /> sometime between [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]] and [[36 BBY/Legends|36 BBY]].<ref name="NEC" /> One Trade Federation [[Power core/Legends|power core]] on the moon was attacked by the predatory [[Gundark/Legends|gundarks]], causing the Federation to abandon that particular area. After the Wookiees arrived on the moon two of their early surveyors, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] and [[Shoran]], encountered and destroyed the power core on the advice of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], who was concerned by the technological presence on a supposedly uncolonized world.<ref name="GB" />

Nute Gunray sent a [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]] named [[OOL-2]] to investigate the ruins of the power core, who reported that it had been destroyed by gundarks. In response Gunray instructed OOL-2 to find and eliminate the gundarks, and to deliver the pelts to their [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] ally [[Pekt]]. A squad of battle droids attacked the [[Unidentified gundark nest|gundark nest]] and had almost finished [[Skirmish at the gundark nest|exterminating]] the creatures when a force of Wookiees led by Chewbacca, who had also been dealing with gundarks, arrived on the scene. The droids attacked the Wookiees, who destroyed them all in response. Afterwards, the focus of the Wookiee [[Alaris Prime colonists|colonists]] shifted from self-sustenance to expanding their military to fight the Trade Federation. Their leader Attichitcuk undertook a [[Scout/Legends|scouting]] mission, sighting a group of battle droids commanded by [[DRN-38]].<ref name="GB" />

[[File:Wookiee_attack.png|thumb|left|350px|The Trade Federation fought a war with the Wookiees for control of Alaris Prime.]]
DRN-38's droids [[Ambush of Attichitcuk|ambushed]] Attichitcuk and shot him along with his entourage. Jinn sensed that the [[Wookiee Chieftain|chieftain]] had survived, so Chewbacca gathered several [[bowcaster trooper]]s and [[Rescue of Attichitcuk|marched]] into Trade Federation territory to find him. Every B1 battle droid encountered by the Wookiees was destroyed, and after Attichitcuk was found and taken to a [[Unidentified Wookiee base (Attichitcuk's rescue)|base]] for safety, DRN-38 sent three droidekas in reprisal, but they too were destroyed. Chewbacca then became the leader of the colonists and led a successful [[Darth Maul/Legends|attack]] against a [[Trade Federation outpost]] commanded by [[GWC-04]], which had been used to produce battle droids. The droid [[LUH-989]] also launched an [[Attack on Chewbacca's camp|attack]] on [[Chewbacca's camp]] using [[Battle Droid Beta Version]]s and [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|beetle droids]]. After that attack was repelled, scouts from [[Shoran's camp]] discovered a [[Trade Federation listening array|listening array]] that the Trade Federation had built to [[Spy/Legends|spy]] on their colonial opponents, which was then [[Attack on the Trade Federation listening array|destroyed]] by the Wookiees.<ref name="GB" />

After the destruction of the listening array, Chewbacca believed it was time to forcefully remove the Trade Federation from Alaris Prime. Their last stronghold was a [[Unidentified Trade Federation base|base]] commanded by [[SRAM-13]], who had a group containing droidekas and beetle droids attack several Wookiee [[Sentry tower/Legends|sentry posts]]. The Wookiees assembled several [[Agr (starfighter)|Agr]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] and [[Energy pummel/Legends|energy pummels]] to destroy the turrets of the base, and after that sent in their infantry forces, including a recovered Attichitcuk, Chewbacca, Shoran, and Qui-Gon Jinn, who had only guided the Wookiees remotely until that point. The [[Battle for Alaris Prime]] saw the destruction of the Trade Federation's fortress, symbolizing the end of their colonization on Alaris Prime.<ref name="GB" /> The war also exposed the Federation's hidden manufacturing operation there.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

=====Terrorist attacks=====
[[File:NebulaFront.svg|thumb|right|250px|The Nebula Front (logo pictured) attacked Trade Federation shipments.]]
In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], Darth Sidious was ready to launch his master plan and declared himself to the Neimoidian faction of the Directorate. Sidious both blackmailed and flattered Gunray into accepting a "partnership", relying on his dissatisfaction with the current Directorate, which he felt did not recognize his talents and stymied his plans. Promising Gunray a "surprise promotion", Sidious dispatched his apprentice [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] to the [[Mining/Legends|mining]] world of [[Dorvalla/Legends|Dorvalla]], where Maul pit the rival companies [[Lommite Limited]] and [[InterGalactic Ore]] against one another. The Trade Federation had long sought to control the planet's [[Lommite/Legends|lommite]] trade, and owing to Maul's actions the two companies merged to form [[Dorvalla Mining]], which soon agreed to allow the Trade Federation to export lommite ore, and to accept Trade Federation representation in the Senate. As a result, Gunray's power was solidified, and so was the hold Sidious had over the Viceroy.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TEA" />

Meanwhile, violence between the [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]] and the Trade Federation was intensifying. In further conversations with the Viceroy, Darth Sidious demanded that the Neimoidians willingly sacrifice one of their ''Lucrehulk''-class freighters, the ''[[Revenue]]'', and its cargo of [[Aurodium/Legends|aurodium]] ingots worth two billion [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. In a second [[Dorvalla Incident|incident at Dorvalla]], a Nebula Front group led by [[Arwen Cohl]] raided the ''Revenue'' and made off with the cargo, which prompted Nute Gunray to again demand the right to increased protection on the Trade Federation's ships.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TEA" />

As Senator Palpatine, Sidious convinced Supreme Chancellor [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Valorum]] that renewed taxation was the only way to check the abuses that produced the dissatisfaction that led to the violence of the Nebula Front. As this would effectively abolish the Free Trade Zones that had made the Trade Federation so wealthy, Senator Lott Dod again raised objections and repeated the demand that the Federation be allowed to expand its droid army to defend against the Nebula Front. Palpatine proposed that a [[Eriadu Trade Summit|summit]] be held on [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] to allow all sides to come to an agreement. Owing to Sidious' manipulations, the summit was an utter disaster: the Trade Federation Directorate's [[Security droid/Legends|security droids]] turned their weapons on their charges, killing the entire Directorate but for Gunray and Dod.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TEA" />

In the aftermath of the disastrous [[Eriadu Trade Summit]], Gunray proceeded to fill up the vacancies on the Directorate with his Neimoidian puppets, some of whom later comprised the [[Trade Federation Occupation Council|Occupation Council]] that took control of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] after the Naboo invasion.<ref name="TNEGTC" />

Showing little sympathy for the Trade Federation after Eriadu, the Galactic Senate became determined to impose taxation, drafting [[Senate Resolution BR-0371]]. The new [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], led the call for new taxation, and Senator Palpatine, knowing it would antagonize the Trade Federation, agreed with his monarch. As Darth Sidious, he contacted Gunray and encouraged him to begin preparations for a [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of Naboo in protest of the resolution.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TEA" />

====The invasion of Naboo====
The Federation procured the necessary resources on a number of planets, including [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]],<ref name="Adventures">''[[Star Wars: Episode I Adventures]]''</ref> and [[Eos]].<ref name="Starfighter" /> Gunray had a brief moment of panic before launching the blockade, fearing the cost of diverting so many ships from trade, though Sidious coldly informed him that any loss of revenues would inevitably be balanced out through the Trade Federation's investors shipping of weapons. Amid the preparations, [[Deputy Viceroy]] [[Hath Monchar]] attempted to reveal the plot to the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], though he was killed by Darth Maul before he could succeed.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /><ref name="NEC" /> Two of the Trade Federations member species&mdash;the [[Caarite]]s and the [[Filordus|Filordi]]&mdash;felt this blockade would destroy the Federation, so they split off to form the [[Metatheran Cartel]] and forced the Federation out of the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]].<ref name="LFCG" />

[[File:Trade_Federation_Droid_Army.png|thumb|left|350px|The Trade Federation's invasion force marches on the Naboo capital of Theed.]]
The Trade Federation's fleet was largely made up of [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|converted ''Lucrehulk''-class freighters]], which included 50 conference rooms on the ships' center sphere for trade negotiations. In large part because of this, the Trade Federation when designing the rooms deliberately gave special adaptations to them to specifically place clients at a disadvantage, including the installation of variable gas emitters as well as remote-operated "concentration deficit" chairs to make it difficult for their clients to think clearly.<ref name="SW:CL" /> The Executive Board was unwilling to spend more credits (being the thrifty businessmen they were), and chose to convert their enormous commercial freight carriers into formidable, three-kilometer long warships, complete with shields, turbolasers, and military grade communications arrays. Also, the Trade Federation struck deals with numerous species, like the [[Colicoid/Legends|Colicoids]] and the [[Xi Char/Legends|Xi Char]], to construct massive armies for the Federation.<ref name="E:ICS" /> Also because of their thriftiness, as well as the development of their droid army around the same time, they also had the air-traffic control rooms for the various ships replace both paid employees and expensive protocol droids with low-maintenance OOM pilot droids to offset the costs.<ref name="SW:CL" />

In addition, even in the long awaited and profitable enterprise of battle, the Trade Federation warcraft were still manufactured inexpensively. Unwilling to spend more money on [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]], the Trade Federation Executive Board controlled their massive armies from a single central control computer aboard a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]].<ref name="SWEI:TPM" />

With Naboo blockaded and beginning to starve, Nute Gunray felt that the Senate would be forced to concede on the issue of taxation. However, while the Senate debated endlessly on the blockade, Supreme Chancellor Valorum secretly requested that two [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] be dispatched to force a settlement. Jedi Master Qui-Gon Jinn and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] arrived on the flagship [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']] and were immediately [[Mission to Naboo|set upon]] by poison [[Dioxis/Legends|dioxis]] gas and battle droids. On the orders of Darth Sidious, Gunray began a general invasion of Naboo in an effort to force the Senate to come to terms, expecting that Queen Amidala would easily be induced to sign a capitulation treaty to legitimize the invasion.<ref name="SWEI:TPM" />

[[File:InvasionOfNaboo.png|thumb|right|300px|The Battle of Naboo]]
The [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] swiftly secured the major cities and Nute Gunray installed himself as leader of an [[Trade Federation Occupation Council|occupation government]] in the capital of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]]. The civilian population was largely interned in makeshift prison camps, and with battle droids having little idea of how to care for human beings, sickness and starvation soon set in.<ref name="EGW-cut6" /> With the aid of Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi, however, Queen Amidala escaped to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] with a small entourage. While she failed to rally the Senate against the Federation, she orchestrated a [[Vote of No Confidence/Legends|vote of no confidence]] against the now largely-powerless Valorum, allowing Naboo's Senator Palpatine to be [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY/Legends|elected]] as his successor.<ref name="SWEI:TPM" />

Returning to Naboo, Amidala unilaterally set aside ancestral differences with the native [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] and formed an alliance. In the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|ensuing battle]], the droid control ship was destroyed and the droid army disabled, while Gunray himself was forced by Amidala to sign a new treaty after trapping him in the throne room. Gunray was forced to make a humiliating return to Coruscant to face a Senate investigation, with Panaka also implying while watching him leave that the results of the Senate's investigation may potentially result in the Trade Federation's shutdown.<ref name="SWEI:TPM" /> It would not be until over a decade later that it was discovered that invasion had in fact been a massive ruse orchestrated by Darth Sidious to elevate his public persona of Palpatine to the office of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]].<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

====Separatist Crisis====
Despite the Naboo expecting that the Senate would revoke the Federation's trade franchise as punishment for the invasion,<ref name="SWEI:TPM" /> the Trade Federation retained much of its power. Despite four trials in the [[Supreme Court/Legends|Supreme Court]], Nute Gunray remained Viceroy.<ref name="SWEII:AOTC" />

Following the Invasion of Naboo, the Federation began diversifying its fleets, with new [[Destroyer/Legends|destroyers]] and [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]] using the modular core ships as control cores.<ref name="AOTC:ICS" /> In addition, [[Pammant Docks/Legends|Pammant Docks]] provided the Trade Federation with massive [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyers]], such as the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']].<ref name="ROTS:ICS">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> They also formed an [[Trade Federation elite assassination corps|elite assassination corps]] to seek revenge on the Jedi, an endeavor that was unsuccessful.<ref name="GB" />

After the collapse of his final trial, Nute Gunray approached [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], who had recently left the Jedi Order over the death of his former apprentice Qui-Gon Jinn on Naboo, and told him what he knew of Darth Sidious. Unbeknownst to Gunray, Dooku had already turned to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] and sworn himself to Sidious as Darth Tyranus.<ref name="SWEII:AOTC" />

From [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]], Count Dooku began rallying various systems and corporations to form the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] on [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]]. Gunray however did not formally align the Trade Federation with the Separatists until the outbreak of war in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. His price for the support of the Trade Federation and its [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|droid army]] was the death of the now-[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], in revenge for his humiliation ten years earlier.<ref name="SWEII:AOTC" />

===Clone Wars===
====Battle of Geonosis====
{{Quote|With these new battle droids we've built for you, you'll have the finest army in the galaxy.|[[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]] to [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], telling how the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] has built one of the strongest armies in galactic history for the Trade Federation|<ref name="SWEII:AOTC" />}}
In 22 BBY on the eve of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Nute Gunray pledged the Trade Federation's resources to said cause in exchange for the death of Padmé Amidala, as revenge for the fiasco on Naboo. Unfortunately, a botched attempt on Amidala's life by [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] resulted in [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] tracking a [[Jango Fett/Legends|bounty hunter]] to [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], where Gunray and the other various members of the CIS had gathered. Kenobi was captured, but this merely resulted in [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and Amidala setting out to rescue Kenobi.<ref name="SWEII:AOTC" />

Eventually, these events spiraled into [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] leading a Jedi attack on the arena where the prisoners were about to be executed, much to Gunray's dismay. Upon [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda's]] arrival with a large [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]], it descended into a full scale battle, starting off the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Confederacy and the Republic.<ref name="SWEII:AOTC" /> The Trade Federation was unable to break off now, and soon Federation automata formed much of the CIS army.<ref name="ROTS:ICS" />

====The course of the war====
The Federation officially claimed neutral status in the Clone Wars, and indeed Lott Dod continued to represent it in the Senate. However, the Federation was clearly a major military and financial contributor to the Confederacy, with Dod taking instructions from Count Dooku. During the [[Battle of Ryloth/Legends|Battle of Ryloth]], Dod deliberately attempted to stymie the Republic's diplomatic efforts towards [[Toydaria/Legends|Toydaria]] to deny it as a staging ground against Separatist forces attacking [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]].<ref name="Supply Lines">{{TCW|Supply Lines}}</ref> The Trade Federation was a major investor in reactivating the [[Geonosis primary droid foundry/Legends|Geonosis droid foundries]], while its [[Blockade of Pantora/Legends|blockade]] of [[Pantora/Legends|Pantora]], ostensibly done in the name of debt collection, was an attempt to force the moon into the CIS.<ref name="Senate Spy">{{TCW|Senate Spy}}</ref><ref name="Sphere">{{TCW|Sphere of Influence}}</ref>

During the course of the war, the planet [[Rosha]] was deeply involved with the Trade Federation.<ref name="TLotJ6" />

While the Trade Federation provided the vast majority of the CIS' military assets, including B1 and [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 battle droids]] and [[Droideka/Legends|Droidekas]], as a business it was highly reluctant to spend more credits than were absolutely necessary to upgrade the droids. Consequently, B1 battle droids were pushed into specialized roles to which they were unsuited, such as [[Warship/Legends|warship]] crewers, [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]], and [[Firefighter droid/Legends|emergency responders]].<ref name="TEGtW" /> Gunray's own dismissive attitude to droids caused him to regard the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies]], [[Grievous/Legends|General Grievous]], as little more than another worker drone. The enraged Grievous nearly killed Gunray before Dooku intervened.<ref name="Labyrinth of Evil">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>

====The end of the conflict====
{{Quote|The war is over! Lord Sidious promised us peace! We only want...|Viceroy Nute Gunray's last words before being killed by Darth Vader|audio=NuteGunraysLastWords.flac|<ref name="SWEIII:ROTS" />}}
Despite several successful offensives such as [[Operation Durge's Lance]], by [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]] the CIS had been forced on to the defensive in the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]]. Trade Federation holdings in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] were besieged by Republic forces, including the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Purse world/Legends|purse-world]] of [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], [[Deko Neimoidia/Legends|Deko Neimoidia]] and [[Koru Neimoidia/Legends|Koru Neimoidia]]. The [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidian homeworld]] itself saw significant fighting, catastrophically affecting the long-term population of the species.<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TEGtW" />

Following the death of Dooku and the Separatists defeat in the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], both of which were orchestrated by Sidious, Nute Gunray, [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]], and the Trade Federation representatives on the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] were evacuated from [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] to a [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility/Legends|secret facility]] on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]. As they had worked with Sidious for well over ten years, Gunray and Haako felt that the Trade Federation had a personal arrangement with Darth Sidious and felt that he would guarantee them peace. Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, however, has issued [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] to fulfill the Sith Order's long-held dream of [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|destroying]] the Jedi Order, was on the point of proclaiming himself, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]. As Sidious, he sent his new apprentice, Anakin Skywalker, now taking the Sith name of Darth Vader, to Mustafar to [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|murder]] the entire Separatist Council and end the Clone Wars, while at the same time he [[Declaration of a New Order|declared]] the Galactic Republic as the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref><ref name="SWEIII:ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Prior to Vader's arrival, Sidious deceived the Separatist Council into believing that Vader would protect them.

On Mustafar, Gunray initially welcomed Vader, who calmly sealed the room and slaughtered the entire Separatist Council, killing Gunray last. Following Gunray's death, Vader ordered the Trade Federation's [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|droid control ships]] to shut down all droid units, ending the Clone Wars.<ref name="SWEIII:ROTS" />

===Reorganization===
====Imperialization====
{{Main|Imperialization/Legends}}

{{Quote|As the Trade Federation signs this treaty of peace with the Empire, we recognize that our constituent parts are no longer under our control. We ask only that the Emperor grant us special dispensation during the distribution of assets in light of our proven track record in business.|Sentepeth Findos|<ref name="RHNSIE" />}}
[[File:Tftreaty.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Sentepeth Findos reluctantly grants the Federation's assets to the Galactic Empire at the end of the Clone Wars.]]
With Nute Gunray's [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|death]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] at the hands of former Jedi Anakin Skywalker, now Darth Vader, the Trade Federation fell.<ref name="SWEIII:ROTS" /> Acting Viceroy [[Sentepeth Findos]] who was on [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]] [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|resisted]] for a [[Battle on Neimoidia/Legends|brief moment]] but was forced by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]] to sign a [[Imperial–Trade Federation treaty|peace treaty]] with the Empire only a few [[Standard day/Legends|days]] after the Clone Wars ended. This gave all of the Federation's resources for the disposal of the Empire and the Federation was placed under the oversight of the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]], where they continued to operate at limited capacity until they [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|sank]] with the Senate in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]. However, there was still [[Trade Federation resistance|some resistance]], whereby [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], when the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] was [[Corellian Treaty|formed]], some former members of the Trade Federation had joined the alliance to [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|free]] the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] of the empire's tyranny, while the rest went their own way.<ref name="RHNSIE" />

====Marath Vooro's resistance====
{{Main|Trade Federation resistance|Five Veils Campaign}}
[[Customs Vizier]] [[Marath Vooro]] refused to accept peace with the Empire and managed to reactivate a number of droids and ships, establishing a short-lived resistance movement based around [[Enarc/Legends|Enarc]] on the [[Five Veils Route/Legends|Five Veils Route]]. Vooro's resistance bolstered the morale of the [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|remaining Separatists]], but he had a critical lack of effective commanders. An Imperial fleet under the command of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Octavian Grant]] decisively defeated Vooro's forces at the [[Battle of Farstine]], then pursued him down the Five Veils Route, ultimately capturing Vooro at the [[Hook Nebula/Legends|Hook Nebula]].<ref name="TEGtW" />

====Association with the Rebel Alliance====
Those few Trade Federation remnants that survived until the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] would enter into associations with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. The [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Trade Defense Force]] Captain [[Blox Hatha]] was refused formal Alliance membership but became a renowned [[Privateer/Legends|privateer]] bearing a Rebel [[Letter of marque/Legends|letter of marque and reprisal]].<ref name="TEGtW" />

Trade Federation holdouts remained after the Battle of Yavin. Fanatical loyalists, zealots, and avengers affiliated with the Trade Federation remained on the planet Naboo, where they were considered enemies of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] and the [[Nal Raka Criminal Empire]] led by [[Borvo]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. In fact, the Nal Raka Criminal Empire assumed control over the [[Old Trade Federation Route/Legends|Old Trade Federation Route]] following the Invasion of Naboo.<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

==Associations==
{{Quote|The Trade Federation cannot function without its head. Neimoidians don't think for themselves. Without the Viceroy to command them, they will cease to be a threat.|[[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]|<ref name="TPMn">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:TF_iconography.png|thumb|250px|Trade Federation iconography]]

===Notable members===
See [[:Category:Trade Federation members|Trade Federation members]].

===[[Battle droid/Legends|Battle droids]]===
The Trade Federation's military forces, by the time of the Naboo Invasion, were primarily composed of battle droids, largely owing to the Neimoidians' major influence in the organization. The most common mainstay of the Trade Federation's mechanized forces were the [[B-series battle droid/Legends|B-series battle droid]], which had been modeled after decayed corpses of Neimoidians as a form of psychological terror. During the Naboo Crisis, the B-series had the B1 battle droid, with the only other variant being the B1 [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|Beetle droid]], named for its insect steed. It would not be until the Clone Wars nearly a decade later that the B-series would include additional variations, including the sniper-wielding [[battle droid assassin]]s, the [[Droid marine]]s (which despite technically being B-series, had green markings akin to the OOM-series) that acted as the last line of defense against boarding, and the B2 super battle droid. The latter droid model was derived from the [[E4 baron droid]], which had originally been designed as an [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] model until being repurposed for guard duty largely because of the Battle of Naboo.

The [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM-series battle droids]] had a similar design to the B-series battle droids, only they were more regulated to duties that rarely involved direct combat situations. There were at least three variants for them that dealt with a different function each. The [[OOM command battle droid/Legends|OOM command battle droid]], who directly led the various units within the Trade Federation's droid armies (and, later, the Confederacy of Independent Systems' droid armies), which were identified by yellow markings on the torso and the head; The [[OOM pilot battle droid/Legends|OOM pilot battle droid]], likewise, functioned as pilots for various war machines for the Trade Federation, from AATs to droid control ships, and had blue shoulders for its identifying characteristics; the [[OOM-series security droid/Legends|OOM security battle droid]], likewise, acted as guard units on either Trade Federation battleships or in conquered territory, and are identifiable via magenta markings on the torso.

The other most prevalent droid model within the Trade Federation were [[Droideka/Legends|Droidekas]], also known as Destroyer droids or wheel droids (the latter due to their form of rapid transportation involving turning into a wheel and speeding towards the opponent), which had been supplied to them at a special rate by the Colicoids in exchange for rare treats. The models were notorious for not only their prowess in battle, but also the fact that their shield generators were powerful enough to withstand even lightsabers, leaving even the Jedi wary of them. There were two variants of the Droideka model. The first, the [[P-series droideka/Legends|P-series destroyer droid]], was under the service of a Central Droid Computer. The second, the more advanced [[W-series droideka/Legends|W-series droideka]], operated in complete autonomy.

Other Trade Federation droid models included the [[Arak-series probe droid|Trade Federation probe]] (which later saw extensive use under General Grievous during the Clone Wars), and the [[turret droid]]s, which included a tripod variation and a specialized variant known as the [[T4 turret droid]].

===Organic forces===
The Trade Federation's armed forces were originally composed of organics, with the [[Trade Defense Force]] being the primary military arm. It was formed as a deterrent against pirates and other ne'er-do-wells. However, like its parent organization, it would grow corrupt and ruthless, exploiting sectors. They also ended up generally replaced by the mechanized forces due to growing Neimoidian influence as a result of the disastrous trade summit. The TDF's officers primarily wore black uniforms, and also commanded several of their ships. The TDF was largely disbanded after the Naboo Crisis was resolved when most of their members were arrested for their role in the invasion, and was eventually disbanded for good with the [[Declaration of a New Order]].

During the Clone Wars, although organics fighting on the ground were rare, organic units did exist, including the [[Neimoidian Gunnery Battalion]] and the [[Neimoidian Home Defense Legion/Legends|Neimoidian Home Defense Legion]]. The latter was formed because the Neimoidians had surprising tenacity regarding protecting their treasures.

===Starfighters===
[[File:VultureDroid-NEGVV.png|thumb|right|130px|A Vulture droid starfighter.]]

Like with its main armed forces, the various Starfighters utilized by the Trade Federation were unmanned. Their most well known Starfighter was the [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|Variable Geometry Self-Propelled Battle Droid, Mark I]], later known as the ''Vulture''-class Battle Droid during the Clone Wars, which had three modes: A ground mode, which allowed them to act as [[Walker/Legends|walkers]], a flight mode, where their wings were closed, and an attack mode where their wings open to reveal cannons inside for Starfighter combat. Although originally non-sentient, by the time of the late Clone Wars, they gained enough sentience to make commands in Neimoidian before doing any maneuvers. There were two other variants used during the Battle of Naboo, the [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|Advanced Droid Starfighter]] and a [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|light version]], which were composed of two wings (one at the bottom) and an airspeeder-like design, respectively. The [[Trade Federation droid bomber]] had a similar design to the ''Vulture''-class, particularly in the "cockpit" (composed of two slit-like "eye" sensors), although it could not transform and was slow and little maneuverability.

Besides the ''Vulture''-class, other Starfighters included the [[Scarab-class starfighter/Legends|''Scarab''-class droid starfighters]] and the E-STAP Starbomber series. The E-STAP series, as indicated by the name, acted as bombers, which had at least three models. [[E-STAP Droid Starbomber|A standard model]], a more [[E-STAP Droid Starbomber|heavily armored version]], and a [[E-STAP Droid Starbomber|shielded version]].

===Ground units===
[[File:PAC.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Trade Federation troop carrier.]]
The artillery for the Trade Federation included the [[AML]] (an anti-air vehicle), the [[AML|HAML]] (an improved version of the AML), the [[Bio cannon]] (a Droideka-like droid functionally similar to the [[Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery|SPHA-T]]), and the [[Heavy Artillery Gun]], alongside its cousins the [[Heavy Artillery Gun|HAG\-M]] and the [[Heavy Artillery Gun|HHAG\-M]] (an improved version of the former).

In addition, the main battle tanks for the Trade Federation were the [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tank]], as well as its more heavily armored cousin, the [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Heavy Armored Assault Tank]]. A smaller version used primarily for hit and run tactics was known as the [[Armored Scout Tank]].

One-droid repulsorlifts known as [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platforms]] were used to scout the area as well as if needs be take out stragglers. A more heavily armed version existed known as the [[Heavy Single Trooper Aerial Platform]]. The [[MVR-3 speeder bike]] served a similar purpose to the STAPs alongside the [[Speeder platform]]s.

The Trade Federation also had access to [[Energy pummel/Legends|Energy Pummels]], siege engines that allowed for breaching into bases. They came in two variants, one having one pummel, and another having two. Due to their being very slow and vulnerable despite being heavily armored, they were often supplied heavy escorts during the time of the Battle of Naboo to compensate.

Aside from the more direct offensive measures, the ground forces also had transport vehicles for delivering their troops. The [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transport]] carried as many as 122 B-series battle droids and/or 20 droidekas. By the time they were refitted during the Clone Wars, they could also carry 12 B2 Battle Droids. A multi-purpose version known as the [[Multi-Utility Transport]] was also used during the Clone Wars, which was capable of carrying large amounts of cargo, although at the cost of its speed, and was an offshoot of the [[Trade Federation Troop Transport]]. The [[Platoon Attack Craft/Legends|Platoon Attack Craft]] was a smaller scale version of the MTT, with the main difference being that it lacked armaments, being purely a troop carrier.

[[OX9]] [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droids]] were frequently used as support regarding developing various bases.

[[Mechanized Assault Flyer]] and [[XT Beetle Transport/Legends|XT Beetle Transports]] were also in use during the Clone Wars.

Although technically spacecraft, the [[Neimoidian trader]] was used to deliver Nova Crystals between Trade Federation bases in occupied territory.

===Aquatic units===
Although rarely used during the Invasion of Naboo, Aquatic units existed during the time of the Naboo Crisis. The [[Ocean Troop Transport]]s were used to deliver troops to underwater combat zones (although, ironically, the OTTs themselves functioned poorly in such environments due to tending to sink) and had an armed version described as battleships, while the [[Trade Federation Patrol Boat]]s were used to guard various prison camps. In addition, their maritime fleets also were composed of various frigates ([[S-FRG]]s, [[S-FRG|S-HFRGs]] and [[S-FRG|S-LFRGs]]), destroyers ([[S-DST]]s and [[S-DST]]s), cruisers ([[S-CRS]]s and [[S-CRS|S-HCRSs]]), and anti-air destroyers ([[S-AAD]]s and [[S-AAD|S-HAADs]]).

During the Clone Wars, their aquatic units have increased somewhat, with their usage of open-air single-droid submarines called [[Mini-sub]]s, aquatic variants of the AATs called the [[Ostracoda-class gunboat|''Ostracoda''-class gunboat]], underwater carriers known as the [[Separatist Sub-Carrier]]s (which had some design similarities to the ''Vulture''-class Starfighter droid), [[Trade Federation submarine|ambush submarines]], and the [[Manta droid subfighter|''Manta'' droid subfighters]].

===Aerial units===
Although comparatively rare, the Trade Federation had some aerial units, including the [[Long Range Air Attack Mechanism]]s and the Mechanized Assault Flyers.

===[[Capital ship/Legends|Capital ships]]===
[[File:Federationbattleship.jpg|thumb|A ''Lucrehulk''-class battleship bearing the markings of the Confederacy of Independent Systems.]]

The Trade Federation's primary battleship (and, at the time of the Naboo Crisis, their only vessel) was the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]], which had been modified from the [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class LH-3210 cargo freighter]]. Two variants existed: A standard battleship, and a specialized version called the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lurehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]] that, as implied by the name, served as the central control ship for the Droid Armies.

The [[Core ship/Legends|Core ships]] were created as a direct response to the end of the Naboo Crisis when the Trade Federation was forced to dismantle their ships. Specifically, it was created as a form of deception, to make the cores of the ''Lucrehulk''-class battleships detachable so that they would only appear to have been dismantled.

Aside from the ''Lucrehulk''-class, the only other capital ships the Trade Federation had access to during the Clone Wars were the [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer]] as well as an [[Trade Federation Cruiser (Second Battle of Lok)|unidentified cruiser model]] used during the [[Battle of Lok (22 BBY)|Second Battle of Lok]].

===Support craft===
Centuries prior to the Naboo Crisis, the Trade Federation had access to the [[LH-3010 capital freighter]], but was eventually decommissioned. Another vessel predating the Naboo Crisis, the [[Trade Federation cargo hauler]]s, had a similar design, although they were specifically stated to be much smaller than the LH-3010.

By the time of the Naboo Crisis, the Trade Federation utilized quad-wing landing ships known as the [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing craft]], with each wing containing a set number of troops and vehicles (eg, 7 Platoon Attack Craft per wing, 24 AATs and 3 MTTs per fore wing, and 33 AATs per aft wing, plus three MTTs in the staging area and two MTTs in the landing pedestal). These vessels were derived in design from the commercial barges in the Federation's merchant fleet. The [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|Trade Federation transport]] had a similar design to the C-9979. Although they formed the basis of the ''Lucrehulk''-class battleships, the [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class LH-3210 cargo freighters]] themselves also saw use in the blockade and later invasion of Naboo. The [[Trade Federation Dropship]] had a similar use to the C-9979s, although in their case, they dropped necessary troops to the battlefield directly instead of landing, with its complement including either two AMTs and six B1 battle droids, or six AATs. In addition, the [[Neimoidian transport]] was used to ferry over organic troops, as unlike most other vessels in the Trade Federation, it was one of the few vessels to specifically transport organic troops instead of droids. The [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle/Legends|''Sheathipede''-class transport shuttles]] were used to deliver Trade Federation VIPs to an occupied world. The Trade Federation also had access to [[Trade Federation escort cruiser|escort cruisers]].

The [[Trade Federation Freighter]] and [[Trade Federation Superfreighter]] acted as cargo delivery vessels, with the latter being an improved version of the former and even having the former dock with it. [[Trade Federation gunship]]s were also utilized. The [[Trade Federation shuttle]] utilized by then-Senator Nute Gunray had some similarities in design to the later Clone Wars-era [[Captor-class heavy munitions cruiser|''Captor''-class heavy munitions cruisers]], although they delivered VIPs as well as Hunter-Killer droids.

The Trade Federation was also rumored to use [[Droch-class boarding ship/Legends|''Droch''-class boarding ships]] during the Clone Wars.

==Behind the scenes==
The Trade Federation is the main antagonist in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], and become a core faction of a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|larger movement]] in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', and [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. Although they had their onscreen debut in ''The Phantom Menace'', their role in Palpatine's rise to power had been indirectly alluded to as early as the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'' Episode IV: ''A New Hope'']], where it mentioned that Palpatine had been aided in becoming President of the Republic by "the massive organs of commerce." Their creation, and to some extent their motives and characterization in ''The Phantom Menace'', had been part of George Lucas's response to the [[Wikipedia:Republican Revolution|Republican Revolution]] in 1994 (which had occurred eight days into Lucas' draft-writing the screenplay for ''The Phantom Menace''), in particular then-Speaker of the House [[Wikipedia:Newt Gingrich|Newt Gingrich's]] [[Wikipedia:Contract with America|''Contract with America'']].<ref name="Republican Revolution's ties to Trade Federation and TPM's plot">Chris Taylor. How Star Wars Conquered the Universe: The Past, Present Future of a Multibillion Dollar Franchise. New York, New York, USA: Basic Books, 2014-2015. Pp. 300-301. "Anyone sitting down to write a screenplay on November 1, 1994, as Lucas apparently did, would have been interrupted eight days into the writing process by one of the most seismic midterm in postwar American history. Republicans took the House and the Senate for the first time in 40 years. A resurgent GOP under House Speaker Newt Gingrich started pushing its tax-cutting, regulation-slashing 'Contract with America.' Democrats, whose messaging had improved since Ted Kennedy's "Star Wars" flub, started calling it a 'Contract On America."<br />"It was perhaps no co-incidence, then, that Lucas started writing about a "Trade Federation," aided and emboldened by corrupt politicians, embroiled in some sort of dispute over the taxing of trade to the outlying star systems. We never learn what the dispute is about -- whether the Trade Federation was pro- or anti-tax. But what we know is that the name of the leader of the Trade Federation -- never actually spoken in the movie, but noted in the script from the start -- was Nute Gunray. By 1997, when the GOP Senate leader was Trent Lott, Lucas named the Trade Federation's representative in the Galactic Senate: Lott Dodd. We're a long way from the subtlety of his [George Lucas's] [North] Vietnam metaphor here."</ref> The article ''The Trade Federation and Neimoidians: A History'', written on October 14, 2014 by [[Tim Veekhoven]], also implied that the [[Wikipedia:Dutch East India Company|Dutch]] and [[Wikipedia:British East India Company|British East India Companies]] played some historical basis for the Trade Federation as well.<ref name="The Trade Federation and Neimoidians: A History">{{SW|url=news/the-trade-federation-and-neimoidians-a-history|text=The Trade Federation and Neimoidians: A History|nolive=1}}</ref>

The Trade Federation's creation date was speculation of [[Time Tales|Michael Potts]]. He chose the date of 350 BBY in his timeline, based on available information, and was pleasantly surprised when his fellow Star Wars Fanboy Association member [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]] used [[Time Tales]] as a reference point when writing [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], and therefore established this date within continuity.

The Trade Federation's backstory and origins were substantially expanded by author [[Jason Fry]] in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''. Fry posited that the Trade Federation had begun as a noble institution with a positive influence on galactic affairs, before becoming a victim of its own success and transforming into the very shipping cartel it had been formed to regulate.<ref name="Warfare endnotes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/22128732052/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-5|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 5}}</ref>
